annotations.title: Get Super PAC Organisation Donor Totals

description: Totals from the Super PAC Donors Register, built from the FEC's bulk files: organisation contributions to super PACs and hybrid PACs for the 2025-26 and 2023-24 cycles, with rows, names as filed, named donors, the reviewed share and each FEC bulk file's date, and the change over the same date window in both cycles; organisation money by reviewed class, with issue and social-welfare groups split between those an exact IRS Exempt Organizations record matches and those whose status was not matched, beside companies, unions, trade associations, committees, tribal governments and other organisations; withheld and unreviewed strings as counts and amounts only; itemized contributions from individuals reported directly to these committees, counted only, beside organisation money on that exact basis, with conduit pass-through rows (ActBlue, WinRed) shown apart and excluded from every total; sectors and the largest recipient committees as the register lists them; the lag line; and the register's headlines with their basis. Organisation, committee and individual money into super PACs are three measures, each labelled and never combined into one figure. Organisation money is not corporate money: every total states its class. Super PACs and hybrid PACs are named exactly as the FEC committee master lists them, with their committee ids and no party or candidate label; a contribution to a super PAC is not a contribution to a candidate. The word nonprofit appears only on a record an exact IRS Exempt Organizations match carries, shown with that record; other issue and social-welfare groups read organisation (status not matched). Every answer carries the register's question note: these records show contributions reported to the FEC; they do not show what any donor received or intended, and they do not show cause and effect. Individual donors are counted, never named; withheld strings (trusts, holding vehicles, businesses named for a person, names resting on initials, unmatched committees) and unreviewed strings appear only as counts and amounts. Every answer quotes the FEC's restriction on the sale or use of individual contributor information (52 U.S.C. 30111(a)(4)) and the FEC bulk file date; the bulk file lags the committees' latest reports.
